messages:
alex: heads-up — i've been looking at the last 24h of queue spikes in eu-west. latency SLOs hit on gen-heavy customers around 11:30-13:00 UTC repeatedly. looks like regional saturation + cross-region retries.

maria: ugh, same. spikes line up with model A rollouts + a handful of big batch jobs. are we still on hard-reject for PIPELINE_TIER=free?

jin: yes, default is reject when pool capacity < 10% to avoid unbounded queues. but i think that policy is punting too many requests to downstream fallbacks and increasing client retries (costly).

alex: proposal: try locality-aware preemptive queueing. quick summary: if local zone saturated but sibling zone has spare capacity, queue briefly (~200ms) and forward to sibling with affinity preemptions rather than immediate reject. if sibling warm pool unavailable, degrade (partial token shed) instead of hard reject.

sarah: can you sketch config? quick snippet would help ops runbook.

jin: sure — rough idea:
```
admit_control:
  mode: locality_preempt_queue
  queue_ms: 200
  preempt_threshold: 0.6  # fraction of client tokens allowed to be preempted
  sibling_routing: true
  degrade_policy:
    token_shed_pct: 30
    min_response_ok: true
```
notes: sibling routing only if network RTT < 30ms and cost_delta < $0.00002/token.

maria: love the RTT+cost guardrails. curious how fairness works — could big customers get punted more?

alex: fairness: add per-customer priority windows and randomized preemption to avoid tail-risk. small customers get faster bypass for short queues.

luke: ops questions: how does this interact with dedicated pools? we can't cross-tenant route there.
jin: dedicated pools stay strict reject. locality_preempt_queue only applies to shared-hosted pools. for dedicated, we can enable a soft-degrade where we shed non-critical tokens (e.g., reduce max tokens or lower sampling temp) but that's per-tenant opt-in.

maria: rollout plan idea:
1) start in canary for <5% traffic in eu-west on model A
2) collect retry, p50/p99 lat, and cost delta vs baseline for 48h
3) if retries drop and cost per request delta < 10%, expand to 25%
4) revert knob to hard-reject if tail error rate increases or p99 latency > SLO + 100ms

ops-bot: automated note — created runbook PR: github.com/redwood/inference/runbooks/admit_preempt_queue.md (for review).

sarah: how do we measure user-facing quality when we degrade? need cheap evals.

alex: add a small synthetic prompt set (10 prompts/user-profile) and monitor semantic drift + perplexity delta. tie alerts to drift > threshold AND increased retries.

jin: also: telemetry change — add fields in trace: admit_mode, routed_to_zone, degraded_pct, preempted_token_count. that'll make rollbacks straightforward.

luke: cost modeling: routing to sibling increases egress and possibly VM hours. maria, can finance run delta for eu-west morning window?
maria: on it — i'll get an overnight estimate and post numbers tomorrow.

alex: decision for now: approve canary test in eu-west for next deploy cycle, jin to own experiment, ops to monitor and have force-revert flag ready. :thumbsup:

maria: noted. i'll coordinate with sales for any enterprise impact comms (dedicated customers unaffected).

jin: i'll push the canary config and add the new telemetry. expected deploy: 2065012400 UTC. will post if anything strange immediately.

ops-bot: deploy-scheduler: canary rollout scheduled at 2065012400. monitor window 2h. alert if p99 latency > baseline + 100ms or error rate increase > 0.5%.

alex: thanks everyone — keep thread updates short. if we see regressions, flip the revert flag and we'll regroup.
